court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: III Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Chennai (O.P.Nos.618 of 2015 & 2274 of 2016)
facts_of_case: The parties were married on 20.11.2013. The husband filed O.P.No.618 of 2015 for dissolution of marriage due to non-consummation, while the wife filed O.P.No.2274 of 2016 for restitution of conjugal rights. The trial court dismissed the husband's petition and allowed the wife's petition.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle their disputes and seek a decree by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: Both the appellant and respondent mutually agrees and prayed for dissolution of marriage conducted between them on 20.11.2013.

legal_principles.principle: A joint memo of compromise can be used to settle disputes and seek a decree.
legal_principles.held: The said Joint Memo of Compromise dated 29.08.2022, duly signed by both the appellant as well as respondent and their respective counsel and prayed for passing of decree of divorce by mutual consent.

outcome.final_order: The marriage was dissolved by mutual consent.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on restitution of conjugal rights
